svg.title: D2 v2 compact dieline 1:1 (mm)
svg.desc: 105 x 118 card, S segment + flanged strut

g.inkscape:label: artwork - REVERSE: black card, lemon type
dimensions + legend
g.text: Card 105 x 118 mm, one piece, square trim (no rounded corners). 21 % smaller than the 105 x 148 v1.
Board: PRE-COLOURED lemon (#feed95) 350-400 g/m2, caliper 0.44-0.50; no flood print, no bleed, cracks at folds stay yellow.
Digital presses mostly stop at 300-350 g: use 350 g (0.44) and check the press; litho / screen for 400 g.
Grain parallel to the 105 mm side = parallel to c1 c2 c3 (and to the 450 mm side of SRA3). All creases scored from the PRINTED face.
Name: Wix Madefor Text Medium 6.8 mm ("Sophia Zhuravkova" = 61.8 mm). Table/seat 4.9 mm type = 3.5 mm caps.
Reverse colourway (hidden layer "artwork_reverse", same die): black through-dyed board, lemon type, see d2_dieline_reverse.svg.
valley 75 deg from flat -> S stands at 75 deg (15 deg back-lean)
valley 135.7 deg -> P stands at 44.3 deg
valley 119.3 deg beyond P -> lip lies on the FRONT face of S, over the crown
2 x 5 mm, 90 deg AGAINST the score (mountain): rise up/back, away from S and table; end 6 mm after c2 and 8 mm before c3
A flat 0.5 mm strut buckles at about 3 N; a C-channel with two 5 mm flanges has ~100x the bending stiffness (see d2_verify.txt),
is still ONE part with ONE hook, and needs only 2 more creases + 4 short slits in the same die.
Twin struts: each strip is narrower (I ~ width) and needs a rung or two hooks; flatter, not stiffer.
Relief: O1.8 cut at each crease end (S: 2, P: 2) + O1 at slit ends: no tear when lifting.
Geometry: b = 40, S crown (8.28, 30.91) from c1, P 44.29 (drawn net; +0.3 for fold take-up if the test says so).
Crease: valley, scored from printed face
